name: Henninger Legacy Homes
headline: Atlantis Community Foundation is building Henninger Legacy Homes, a four-story, 60-unit permanent supportive housing building for people experiencing homelessness, people with disabilities and veterans, on Bayaud Enterprises' former headquarters site in Denver's Baker neighborhood, with a $1,450,000-a-year 2023 Round One 9% credit award from CHFA.
why_it_matters: It pairs a nonprofit landowner's $0 site sale (in exchange for new office space in the building) with a forgivable 99-year Denver loan and rental subsidy on every unit (VASH, Section 811 and Section 8), a template for supportive housing on a service provider's own land.

status.label: Under construction (reported February 2026); opening slated for 2026, not yet confirmed
status.detail: Denver approved a $3M loan on 2024-10-14 with a June 10, 2025 closing deadline; in December 2024 Atlantis said construction would start that month for a spring 2026 opening. Naked Denver reported construction under way on 2026-02-06, and Atlantis's property page lists the project as under construction and scheduled to open in 2026. No dated closing, completion or lease-up record was found.

next_step: Watch for a certificate of occupancy, a grand opening notice from Atlantis or Bayaud Enterprises, and CHFA's placed-in-service record.

key_numbers.meaning: Every unit is subsidized: 10 HUD-VASH, 15 Section 811 PRA and 35 Section 8 vouchers, per Denver's request memo.

background.text: Atlantis Community Foundation, created in 1998 by the disability-rights nonprofit Atlantis Community Inc., had already turned its Baker holdings into 144 units of tax credit housing; this is its third recent LIHTC project, two blocks from the other two.

The application's service model centers on employment: three case managers and a mental health counselor, then job training and placement through Bayaud Enterprises, whose program offices and food bank move into the building.

Denver City Council's South Platte River Committee approved the $3M loan by consent on 2024-09-04 and the full council adopted resolution CR24-1126 on 2024-10-14; the loan requires a 99-year covenant at 30% AMI.

In December 2024 Atlantis said construction would begin that month with a groundbreaking in January and about 14 months of work, for a spring 2026 opening; Bayaud's offices moved to Lakewood during construction.
Market study and site findings in the application: lease-up expected in about two months, no vacancies at surveyed LIHTC properties, and an environmentally clean, flat infill site.

discrepancies.text: CHFA lists the address as 333 W. Bayaud Avenue, Denver's loan papers give 313 W. Bayaud Ave and 90 S. Elati St, and Atlantis's property page gives 473 W. Bayaud Ave.
The application and CHFA's award description name Bayaud Enterprises as lead service provider, while Atlantis's current property page and Naked Denver name ServiceSource.
The application planned Archway Housing as property manager, while Atlantis's property page lists Brothers Property Management.
The application says all units will have project-based Section 8 vouchers, while Denver's memo splits subsidy among 10 VASH, 15 Section 811 PRA and 35 Section 8 vouchers.
